### Reading Comprehension — Questions 96–100

Read the passage carefully.

Scientific findings gain credibility when other researchers can inspect the methods and attempt to reproduce the results. Open-source software can support this process, but merely publishing the code does not guarantee reproducibility. Researchers must also document software versions, dependencies, data-cleaning decisions and analytical parameters. Without these details, identical code may produce different outputs when executed in different environments. Reproducibility is therefore not simply an act of sharing files; it is a discipline of recording decisions and making analytical workflows transparent.
questions.explanation: The correct expression is “averse to”.
